text:
tori_sales: Heads-up — OrchidPay wants a drop-in transition from CompetitorX. POC kickoff tomorrow 10am PT. They need answers on compatibility, pricing tiers for committed tokens, and the security questionnaire before we demo.
ben_engineer: Quick compatibility note — they rely on a header-based streaming pattern using `X-Stream-Token` + chunked SSE. We don't have that exact header today but can proxy/translate in the adapter layer. Should be doable for POC. @priya_se can you confirm any behavioral deltas we should flag? :thinking:
priya_se: For prompt parity, main gotchas are how the competitor pads system messages and their default sampling params. We'll need to provide a mapping doc and a small test harness. Minimal changes: map system prompt -> system, pass `temperature=0.2` by default for their use-case.
josh_infra: Orchids asked for static egress IPs for staging and a CIDR allowlist for their firewall. We can give them the dedicated staging pool (static-ips-approx) but need legal signoff for outbound peer-to-peer traffic. CC @mike_security.
mike_security: I uploaded the redacted security bundle and SOC2 certificate link to the shared drive. Also asked for answers to their vendor security questionnaire (30 Qs) — I'll take the first pass, but need their specific KMS/HSM requirements.
priya_se: For response differences: they do prefix-trimming and a small post-process that removes repeated salutations. Recommend we add a post-processing shim in the POC to reduce perceived drift.
ben_engineer: For the adapter, here's a quick curl we can hand to their engineers to emulate CompetitorX calls against our POC shim:
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -H 'X-Stream-Token: abc123' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-compat-v1","prompt":"<user_prompt>","max_tokens":512}' \\
  https://staging.redwood.example.com/compat/stream
```
tori_sales: Great, include that in the kickoff deck. On pricing: OrchidPay expects a committed discount schedule and wants to compare per-1k-token rates. @finance_bot can you paste the quick math for committed 1M tokens/mo vs on-demand?
finance_bot: Baseline on-demand: $0.06 / 1k input+output tokens. Committed 1M/mo -> tier1 20% discount -> $0.048 / 1k. If they commit 3M -> tier2 35% discount -> $0.039 / 1k. Also note Dedicated contract available for strict latency/SLA (addl platform fee).
tori_sales: Perfect. I'll surface the numbers and note the adapter engineering effort as a one-time services line item.
mike_security: One blocker to call out pre-demo: OrchidPay wants FIPS-verified KMS for production keys. We can do POC with customer-managed keys in our staging KMS but will need private deployment conversations for FIPS.
ben_engineer: Timeline: we can have the translation shim up in staging in ~48 hours (small proxy + post-process). We'll add a smoke test set of 20 prompts for prompt-parity validation.
priya_se: I'll draft the mapping doc and the 20-prompt smoke tests tonight and link in this thread.
tori_sales: Thanks team — please drop links here as you add them. I'll loop in OrchidPay CISO and their engineering lead after we confirm the static IPs and the security Q answers. :+1:
